verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Vapi API/generic units with USFDA-compliant plants, diversified customers and proven working-capital discipline; avoid single-customer, single-molecule and China-import-dependent borrowers.
title: Vapi Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Vapi pharma unit buys KSMs and intermediates, runs multi-step chemical synthesis, and sells bulk APIs or generic formulations to formulators and exporters.** Cash comes in on export/domestic formulation sales; cash goes out early on raw material, solvent and power. Vapi GIDC hosts bulk-drug plants — one local report describes Vital Labs producing hydroxychloroquine sulphate bulk drug at scale in Vapi GIDC [2], though that source is from April 2020 and should be read as background only. **Gujarat holds one-third of India's pharma output [1], so the cluster is real; but the sources say little about Vapi-specific current capacity, so lean on first principles and peer results.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the USFDA-approved plant and the filed dossier, not the molecule.** The US $63.7 billion of small-molecule drugs losing exclusivity in the US between 2025-29, 65% more than the previous cycle, is the demand pull [1]. **Cash, however, sits in receivables and inventory.** Peer rating work shows working-capital intensity of 47-48% at Concord Biotech even after improvement from 77% in FY2018 [9], and Cohance Lifesciences ran fund-based limits of ₹420 crore with utilisation falling from 70-90% to 40-50% in Q1FY25 [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check receivable days and inventory holding first; if inventory exceeds 90 days, ask which molecules are slow-moving and who the customer is.**

## What has changed now
**The demand signal is strong but the macro is not.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of ₹613 crore in Q2 FY27, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% from 17.7% [3][5]; RPG Life Sciences grew Q2 FY27 revenue 16.5% to ₹211.6 crore [6] and targets 25% API growth [4]. **Against that, India-wide output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY [D] — a 23.7 pp gap that says money is chasing slower real activity.** Gujarat GST collections are +11.9% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. **So when a proposal lands, check whether growth is volume-led or credit-funded; if the borrower's sales growth outruns its power consumption and debtor days are rising, ask for the customer-wise sales register.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue mid-size API and complex-generic units with at least two USFDA-approved sites, diversified customers and a CDMO or LoE-linked order book.** Aarti's CDMO expansion and Xanthine capacity ramp-up [5] and RPG's 25% API growth target [4] show where the peer money is going. **Avoid single-customer contract-research units and China-import-dependent single-molecule plants.** ICRA flags modest scale — ₹61.0 crore FY2024 revenue — and high customer concentration as live risks [7], and China supplied 65-70% of India's API imports [10]. **So when a proposal lands, check import dependence and top-customer share; if one customer exceeds 30% of sales or China-sourced KSM exceeds half of input cost, ask for the alternate-source plan.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the fixed asset.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, quarterly CMA data, and a charge on receivables. **Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, power bills, and GST returns.**
watch: Debtor days rise above 90 -> ask for customer-wise ageing and hold further disbursement
GST turnover falls below reported sales -> seek explanation and re-rate limit
Power consumption falls while sales rise -> ask for production records
China-sourced KSM share rises above half of input cost -> ask for alternate-source plan
Rating downgrade or outlook change -> review limit and covenants
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
